binders: A finite index type ι; a measurable sample space Ω with a probability measure μ; a family X:ι→Ω→ℝ; a real bound K; and a real threshold t.
hypotheses: Every X_i is measurable and integrable.
Almost surely, |X_i-E X_i|≤K for every i.
The family X is jointly independent.
conclusions: With σ²=∑_i E[(X_i-E X_i)²], if σ²=0 then the upper-tail event {∑_i(X_i-E X_i)≥t} has probability zero.
If σ²>0, that event has probability at most exp(-(σ²/K²)h(Kt/σ²)), where h(u)=(1+u)log(1+u)-u.
mathematical_definitions: E X_i is the Bochner integral of X_i.
σ² is the finite sum of centered second moments.
The probability is the real conversion of the measure of the upper-tail event.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a finite independent family of measurable integrable real random variables whose centered versions are uniformly bounded by K>0, every positive upper-tail threshold has probability zero when the centered variance sum is zero, and otherwise satisfies the exact Bennett exponential bound.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is finite and may be empty.
Only the upper tail is stated.
K and t are strictly positive.
The positive-variance formula is guarded by σ²>0, so no division by zero occurs; the zero case is explicit.
The conjunction is syntactically silent for σ²<0, but σ² is a sum of integrals of squares and hence nonnegative.
The logarithm argument is positive in the positive-variance branch.
The real conversion of event measure is lossless for a probability measure.
